# Warcraft model format and animation references

Author: MiYu. Native Rust reader and sampler: `crates/mengine-assets/src/mdx/`.
The host consumer is `crates/mengine-editor-host/src/warcraft_model.rs`.

- [Darithos/W3ModelViewer](https://github.com/Darithos/W3ModelViewer), pinned at `4fe46a0772520fc7b55078bf32cda1237d1b5f2e`: `MdxReader.cs`, `MdxAnimator.cs`, `MdxModel.cs` and replaceable texture definitions. The native implementation follows the classic record layouts, source track interpolation, pivot transforms and matrix groups. Copyright and permission are retained in `LICENSE-W3ModelViewer.txt`.
- [flowtsohg/mdx-m3-viewer](https://github.com/flowtsohg/mdx-m3-viewer), pinned at `2ff0bc00c6363f425016e23d88c0fb2929d3b3cc`: `src/parsers/mdlx/{genericobject,eventobject,collisionshape}.ts` confirm that event and collision records follow a bare generic node. Copyright and permission are retained in `LICENSE-mdx-m3-viewer.txt`.

- The same pinned mdx-m3-viewer source `src/viewer/skeletalnode.ts` defines accumulated parent quaternion cancellation for `DontInheritRotation`. The native sampler tracks rotation only when a model uses this flag and preserves inherited pivot displacement and scale. Billboard parents use their sampled camera basis. Translation/scale non-inheritance, camera anchoring and a single node combining billboarding with rotation non-inheritance remain explicit unsupported cases.

- Classic layer state follows the same pinned `src/viewer/handlers/mdx/{layer,filtermode}.ts` and `shaders/sd.frag.ts`: explicit RGBA source/destination factors, depth-test and depth-write flags, and cutoffs for alpha-test/modulate modes. Filters3 and4 both use source-alpha/one in this reference. Native states use separate pipeline keys; existing engine coverage-alpha blends retain their defaults. The reference defines a reproducible consumer boundary and does not prove original Warcraft visual parity. GPU checks are tracked in the current native-loading test batch.

No upstream executable, .NET runtime, JavaScript viewer or game model is bundled for native loading. The independent .NET sampler remains a development reference under the existing offline import tooling; it is not invoked by the native reader or host consumer. Original MDX and BLP resources remain in the user-provided game/map archives.

To update the references, pin the new Git commit, retain its license, compare the relevant record and sampling semantics, update `source-info.json` hashes, then run the targeted native fixtures and compare a small real source model with independent source poses. Keep original model captures and reference JSON under `tmp/docs-artifacts/`; do not commit them. Version800 is currently implemented. Reforged layouts, MDL text, effects playback, remaining inheritance combinations, remaining material ordering and environment mapping and full map-selector/game integration remain separate implementation work.

The independent C++20 client in `watcher/war3` consumes the pinned PRE2 emitter/particle/atlas and attachment references listed in `source-info.json`. Its parser retains source emission tracks and attachment names, and the D3D9 consumer owns separate live particle state per scene instance. The MIT copyright and permission remain in `LICENSE-mdx-m3-viewer.txt`. PREM, ribbon strips, child attachment models, environment-fog behavior and original GPU fidelity remain tracked client work.
